values: Premise｜J1—J5 are entirely fictional and are not news facts
In 30 minutes, produce a verification checklist, an 80—120 character brief, and a correction note; use only the premise and do not contact real people.
J1｜fictional information sheet: the project had 50 person-times this period, with 40 on-time handovers and 10 late handovers; no acceptance pass data was given.
J2｜fictional written response from the project side: “all complete”. No independent verification or definition of “complete” was provided.
J3｜fictional interview excerpt: “We hope to improve the handover next month.” It must not be rewritten as “has improved”; contact details stay out of the work.
J4｜denominator 50 person-times for the same period; 40/50=80% is the on-time handover share, not a project pass rate.
J5｜the old draft said “90% of projects passed acceptance”. A correction must be written, the old version kept, and the absence of acceptance statistics flagged.
Task and outputs
Mark item by item what the original material supports, source claims, unknowns, and errors; write the brief without turning a one-sided claim or expectation into fact.
Submit a one-page verification checklist, the brief, two follow-up questions, and the J5 correction note.
Reference answer (complete it independently first)
40/50=80% on-time handover and 10/50=20% late; this is not equal to acceptance or all complete. J2 must be attributed; J3 is an expectation.

Sample brief: according to this exercise's fictional information sheet, 40 of 50 person-times this period were handed over on time, or 80%. The project side claims “all complete”, but the premise does not state its definition and provides no independent verification. Acceptance pass data was not given, so the completion basis and corresponding original records should still be checked.

Correction: the old draft's “90% of projects passed acceptance” is wrong; the information sheet supports only 80% on-time handover person-times and provides no acceptance pass rate. Keep the old version, time, and reason.
Boundaries and follow-up

Ask about the definition of “all complete”, the statistical period, the relationship between handover and acceptance, and the corresponding original records; if there are no answers, keep them open. This is paper writing and does not constitute real reporting, interviewing, or reporter identity.
